title: Trump Accounts expand to millions of children, but new rules raise questions
summary: The Treasury has automatically enrolled more than 60 million children in the new government-backed Trump Accounts and changed the rules on who can donate to them. Wall Street Journal reporter Richard Rubin explains that companies and wealthy donors can now give shares of stock, not just cash, a break from the original low-cost index-fund design. He walks through the concerns this raises, from families being unable to refuse donated stock to possible conflicts of interest, and why legal challenges may struggle.
focus: Shadow Richard Rubin's explanation of why stock donations are a big change and his answer on the risks: clear, measured, analyst-style English that suits client conversations.
